Product description

1ml, 1cc and 100-unit syringes explained

These 1ml U100 30G x 8mm insulin syringes combine a full 1ml barrel with a U-100 insulin scale. In U-100 terminology, 1ml contains 100 units, which is why the same format may also be described as a 1cc insulin syringe or 100-unit syringe. The printed unit scale is the measurement to follow when drawing up insulin; it should always match the concentration shown on the insulin label.

The attached needle is specified as 30G × 8mm. Gauge describes needle thickness: a higher gauge number indicates a thinner needle. Length is a separate measurement, and 8mm is equivalent to approximately 5/16 inch. The appropriate insulin syringe size, gauge and needle length depend on the medicine, dose and injection technique recommended by a healthcare professional.

1ml U100 insulin syringes / Insulin syringe guide

Insulin syringe guide

U-100 insulin syringes to ml: size and gauge guide

Learn how U-100 insulin syringe conversion works, how to read the scale, and how barrel capacity, needle gauge and needle length describe different insulin syringe sizes.

How insulin syringe sizes are described

An insulin syringe is described by three separate measurements: barrel capacity, concentration scale and needle size. Capacity tells you the volume the barrel can hold. The concentration scale tells you which insulin strength the printed unit marks are designed for. Needle size combines gauge, which describes thickness, with length, which describes how far the needle extends.

For the product shown on this site, the complete description is 1ml U-100 30G × 8mm. That means a 1ml barrel, graduations intended for U-100 insulin, a 30 gauge needle and an 8mm needle length. These terms are not interchangeable: “1ml” does not tell you the gauge, and “30G” does not tell you the concentration scale.

Different insulin syringe sizes are available because prescribed doses vary. A smaller barrel can spread a lower number of units across more of the printed scale, which some people find easier to read. A larger 1ml barrel is designed to hold up to 100 units of U-100 insulin. Capacity alone is not a recommendation; the right size is the one that matches the medicine, dose and technique advised by your healthcare team.

U-100 insulin syringes to ml conversion

U-100 insulin contains 100 units in each millilitre. The conversion follows directly from that concentration: divide the number of U-100 units by 100 to express the same volume in millilitres. The safest everyday approach is still to use a matching U-100 syringe and read its unit scale, rather than perform a fresh calculation for every dose.

For U-100 insulin

100 units = 1ml

Volume in ml = prescribed U-100 units ÷ 100

U-100 units

The table explains the relationship between U-100 units and volume; it is not a dosing guide. Never use it to decide how much insulin to take. Follow the prescribed number of units and the instructions supplied with your medicine and device.

U-40 vs U-100 insulin syringes

U-40 and U-100 describe different insulin concentrations. U-40 insulin contains 40 units per millilitre, while U-100 contains 100 units per millilitre. Syringes made for each concentration carry different scales so that a printed unit mark corresponds to the intended volume for that insulin strength.

U-100 syringe

Calibrated for insulin containing 100 units per ml. A full 1ml U-100 syringe corresponds to 100 units on its scale.

U-40 syringe

Calibrated for insulin containing 40 units per ml. Its unit marks represent different volumes from those on a U-100 syringe.

Do not interchange the scales. Using a U-40 syringe with U-100 insulin, or a U-100 syringe with U-40 insulin, can produce a serious dosing error. Confirm the concentration on both the insulin label and syringe wrapper before use.

An insulin syringe conversion between U-40 and U-100 is not a substitute for the correct matching device. If the medicine and syringe do not show the same concentration, stop and ask a pharmacist or clinician for the correct syringe.

What size insulin syringe should you choose?

“Size” can refer to barrel capacity, needle length or both, so it helps to separate the question. Start with concentration compatibility: a U-100 syringe is designed for U-100 insulin. Then consider a barrel capacity that can hold the prescribed number of units without exceeding its scale. Finally, confirm the needle length and technique recommended for you.

Barrel capacity
What the full U-100 scale represents
0.3ml

This comparison describes capacity, not the exact increment between graduation lines. Graduation patterns can differ by product, so check the supplied syringe and manufacturer instructions rather than assuming every barrel of the same size uses the same spacing.

Which size insulin syringe is easiest to read?

A barrel that is only as large as the prescribed dose requires may place the relevant unit range across more of the visible scale, but readability also depends on the printed graduations, contrast, dexterity and eyesight. Ask a healthcare professional which size is suitable, particularly if you have difficulty seeing or handling the markings.

Different types of insulin syringes

Insulin syringes may differ in capacity, concentration calibration, graduation spacing, needle gauge, needle length, fixed or detachable needle design, safety features, packaging and manufacturer. Pen needles and insulin pens are different delivery systems, even when their needle measurements look similar. Select the exact device format prescribed or recommended for your medicine and technique.

What gauge insulin syringe should you choose?

Needle gauge describes diameter. The numbering works in the opposite direction many people expect: a higher gauge number generally means a thinner needle. A 30G needle is therefore finer than a 29G needle. Gauge does not describe length or barrel capacity, and it does not by itself determine which syringe is clinically appropriate.

Measurement
What it tells you
Gauge (G)
Needle thickness; higher gauge numbers generally indicate thinner needles
Length (mm or inches)
How far the needle extends; 8mm is approximately 5/16 inch
Capacity (ml, cc or units)
How much the barrel holds; separate from needle dimensions

When comparing which gauge insulin syringe to use, do not choose from gauge alone. Needle length, injection angle, skin-fold technique and individual needs all matter. A clinician or diabetes nurse can advise on the combination appropriate for you.

How to read an insulin syringe

Reading an insulin syringe correctly begins before drawing up medicine. Work in good light, check the labels and use the printed unit scale intended for the insulin concentration. The steps below explain the reading process in general terms; they do not replace the instructions supplied with your device or training from your healthcare team.

Confirm the insulin concentration

Read the insulin label and identify the concentration, such as U-100. Do not continue if you cannot confirm it.

Match the syringe scale

Check the wrapper and barrel. U-100 insulin requires a U-100 syringe; a different scale is not interchangeable.

Identify the graduation interval

Inspect the numbered marks and the smaller lines between them. Use the manufacturer’s instructions to confirm what each line represents.

Find the prescribed unit mark

Locate the number of units prescribed to you. Do not estimate between markings that the syringe is not designed to measure.

Read at eye level

Hold the barrel where the scale is clear and reduce parallax by viewing the markings straight on rather than from above or below.

Use the correct plunger edge

Align the leading edge of the plunger stopper with the required unit line, following the diagram in the device instructions.

If the marks are difficult to see, the plunger does not align clearly or the device appears damaged, do not guess. Use a new syringe and ask a pharmacist or clinician for help choosing a format you can read reliably.

Storage, single use and sharps disposal

Keep unused syringes in their original packaging, away from damage, moisture and extremes of temperature, and follow the storage conditions printed by the manufacturer. Inspect the wrapper before use. Do not use a syringe if the packaging is open, damaged or beyond any printed expiry date.

An insulin syringe is a single-use medical device. Reuse can damage the needle and may increase contamination or dosing risks. Place the complete syringe straight into an approved sharps container after use. Do not put loose needles or syringes in household recycling or general rubbish. Local collection arrangements vary, so ask your pharmacy, council or healthcare provider how filled sharps containers are handled in your area.

UK buying FAQ

Buying insulin syringes in the UK: questions answered

Direct answers on over-the-counter availability, prescriptions, ordering, choosing a product and disposing of used insulin syringes safely.

Can you buy insulin syringes over the counter in the UK?

Insulin syringes are generally available from UK pharmacies and online medical-supply retailers without a separate prescription for the syringe. Ask a pharmacist to confirm that the concentration scale, capacity, gauge and needle length match the insulin and technique prescribed for you.

Availability and local sales policies can vary. Bring the name and concentration of the insulin when asking for advice, and compare the exact product details on the wrapper rather than relying on colour alone. The syringe scale must match the insulin concentration.

Do I need a prescription to buy insulin syringes?

A prescription is generally not required to buy the syringe itself in the UK. Insulin is a separate medicine and may be supplied on prescription. Always match a U-100 syringe with U-100 insulin and follow the directions from your clinician, pharmacist and product instructions.

A retailer may still apply its own checks or quantity limits. If a particular syringe is part of your NHS supply arrangement, ask your GP practice, diabetes team or pharmacy how to obtain the correct item through that route.

Where can I buy insulin syringes?

You can usually buy insulin syringes from community pharmacies, specialist medical-supply retailers and established UK online shops. Choose a seller that provides the manufacturer, product code, concentration scale, capacity, gauge, needle length, pack quantity, VAT position, delivery terms and returns information.

For online orders, check that the listing describes the same device shown in its photographs. Do not treat generic photos or copied marketplace text as proof of sterility, materials or manufacturer. Verify product claims against the packaging and supplier documentation.

How do I order insulin syringes online?

First confirm the insulin concentration, then choose a matching syringe scale, suitable barrel capacity, needle gauge and needle length. Select the pack quantity, review the total price and delivery terms, and check the product specification again before completing the retailer’s secure WooCommerce checkout.

On this design, the pack selector offers 10, 30, 50 and 100 syringes. The prices are draft placeholders for the future store owner to replace; they are not current offers. The live WordPress version should show confirmed stock, delivery estimates and the final VAT-inclusive total.

Which size insulin syringe should I buy?

Choose a syringe whose concentration scale matches your insulin and whose barrel can hold the prescribed number of units. This featured 1ml U-100 syringe holds up to 100 U-100 units and uses a 30G × 8mm fixed needle, but suitability should be confirmed professionally.

Smaller U-100 barrels may be available for lower maximum doses. The exact spacing of graduation marks can vary, so read the manufacturer instructions rather than assuming every syringe of the same capacity has identical increments. See the insulin syringe sizes and gauge guide for a fuller comparison.

What does 30G × 8mm mean?

“30G” is the needle gauge, a measure of thickness; higher gauge numbers generally indicate thinner needles. “8mm” is the needle length, equivalent to approximately 5/16 inch. Neither figure describes the 1ml barrel capacity or the U-100 concentration scale.

Gauge and length are different choices, and neither should be selected from comfort claims alone. Use the dimensions recommended by your clinician or diabetes team and follow the injection technique supplied with your medicine and device.

Can U-40 and U-100 syringes be used interchangeably?

No. A U-40 syringe is calibrated for insulin containing 40 units per millilitre, while a U-100 syringe is calibrated for 100 units per millilitre. Mixing the syringe and insulin concentrations can cause a serious dosing error, even when the barrels look similar.

Check both labels before every use. If the insulin concentration and syringe scale do not match, stop and ask a pharmacist or clinician for the correct device. Do not improvise a conversion as a substitute for a matching syringe.

How should used insulin syringes be disposed of?

Put each used syringe straight into an approved sharps container. Do not recap it unless your healthcare professional has specifically trained you to do so, and never place loose sharps in household recycling or general waste. Ask your local pharmacy, council or healthcare provider about collection arrangements.

Keep the sharps container upright, secure and out of reach of children. Follow its fill line and closing instructions. Disposal services differ by area, so confirm the local process before the container is full.

What should I check when the order arrives?

Check the product name, code, U-100 scale, 1ml capacity, 30G × 8mm needle specification, pack count and packaging condition against your order. Confirm any expiry or lot information shown, and contact the retailer before use if the item differs or a wrapper is damaged.

Packaging and branding can change, so a visual difference is not automatically a defect. It does mean the item should be checked against the supplier’s current documentation. Do not use any syringe whose individual sterile barrier is open or compromised.

Privacy policy

How personal information would be handled when this design is connected to a live UK ecommerce store.

Launch draft: this static preview does not take orders, payments or contact details. The store operator must add its legal identity, contact details, service providers and retention periods before publishing this policy on a live WooCommerce site.

Information a live store may collect

When you place an order or contact the retailer, the store may collect your name, billing and delivery address, email address, telephone number, order details and correspondence. Payment-card details should be processed by the selected payment provider rather than stored directly by the retailer.

Technical information may include device and browser details, IP address, security logs, cookie preferences and basic information about how the site is used. A live cookie banner should explain any analytics, advertising or preference cookies before they are set.

Why information is used

  • To process and deliver orders, issue confirmations and handle returns.
  • To answer questions and provide customer support.
  • To prevent fraud, protect the website and keep required financial records.
  • To send marketing only where a valid consent or other lawful basis applies.

The final policy should identify the lawful basis used for each purpose and explain whether providing particular information is required to fulfil an order.

Who information may be shared with

Only providers needed to run the shop should receive relevant information, such as the payment processor, hosting provider, delivery carrier, email platform and professional advisers. The live policy must name or clearly describe those providers and explain any transfers outside the UK.

Retention and security

Personal information should be kept only for as long as it is needed for the stated purpose, legal obligations, dispute handling and fraud prevention. The live store should use appropriate access controls, software updates, encrypted connections and tested backups. No website can promise absolute security.

Your data protection rights

Depending on the circumstances, UK data protection law may give you rights to access, correct, erase or restrict use of your information, object to certain processing, or request a portable copy. The final policy must provide a working privacy contact and explain how to complain to the Information Commissioner’s Office.

Policy updates

The live policy should show its effective date and be updated whenever the retailer changes its checkout, providers, cookies or data practices. Last reviewed for this design: 29 September 2026.

Terms & conditions

The proposed terms for ordering products through the future UK online shop.

Launch draft: no purchase can currently be completed through this static preview. Before trading, add the retailer’s legal name, registered or trading address, company and VAT details where applicable, contact channels and final checkout terms.

About these terms

These terms would apply to purchases made through the live store. They should be read with the privacy policy and delivery and returns policy. Nothing in the final terms should limit rights that cannot lawfully be excluded under UK consumer law.

Product information

The retailer should take reasonable care to describe each product accurately, but packaging and branding may change. Customers must check the product name, concentration scale, capacity, gauge, needle length, pack count, wrapper condition and any expiry information when the order arrives.

This site provides general product information, not medical advice. Customers must use the syringe only with a matching insulin concentration and follow the prescribed dose, product instructions and advice from a qualified healthcare professional.

Prices, payment and orders

The live store should display the final price, VAT position, delivery charge and accepted payment methods before an order is submitted. An order acknowledgement does not necessarily mean the order has been accepted; the final terms must explain when the sales contract is formed and what happens if stock or pricing information is incorrect.

Availability and substitutions

Products should not be substituted without the customer’s agreement. If an item is unavailable, the retailer should explain the available options and provide any refund due through the original payment method.

Safe and lawful use

Products must not be resold, altered or used for an unlawful purpose. The retailer may cancel or limit an order where reasonably necessary to comply with law, prevent fraud or protect customer safety, subject to applicable consumer rights.

Liability and complaints

The final terms should explain the retailer’s responsibilities for foreseeable loss caused by breach, while preserving liability that cannot legally be excluded. A clear postal or email contact must be provided for complaints, together with the expected response process.

Changes and governing law

The terms in force when an order is accepted should apply to that purchase. The completed version should identify the governing law and courts appropriate to the retailer and customer. Last reviewed for this design: 29 September 2026.

Customer care

Delivery & returns

What customers should be told about dispatch, delivery, cancellations and product problems before checkout.

Launch draft: delivery regions, services, prices, cut-off times, dispatch estimates, returns address and contact details still need to be confirmed by the retailer. Draft prices elsewhere on this site are not live offers.

Delivery information

The live checkout should show the delivery services available for the entered UK address, their cost and the estimated delivery window before payment. Dispatch and delivery estimates should be realistic and should identify any locations that attract a surcharge or cannot be served.

Customers should receive an order confirmation and a dispatch update where tracking is available. Delays caused by an incomplete address, failed delivery attempt or an event outside the retailer’s reasonable control should be communicated promptly.

Changing or cancelling an order

Customers should contact the retailer as soon as possible if an order needs to be changed or cancelled. If dispatch has already begun, the returns process and any statutory cancellation rights will apply. The final policy must explain the cancellation window and any lawful exclusions relevant to sealed healthcare or hygiene products.

Returns

Before launch, the retailer must state the return period, how to request a return, who pays return postage, the condition required and the return address. For safety, any restriction on returning a sealed product after its sterile or hygiene seal has been broken must be explained clearly before purchase and applied consistently with UK consumer law.

Damaged, incorrect or faulty items

Customers should inspect the outer parcel and individual wrappers when the order arrives. If an item is damaged, incorrect, short-dated or otherwise not as described, it should not be used. The customer should contact the retailer promptly with the order details and photographs where helpful, keeping all packaging until the issue is resolved.

Nothing in the final policy should reduce legal rights for goods that are faulty, not as described or unfit for their normal purpose.

Refunds

Approved refunds should be returned to the original payment method. The live policy must explain expected processing times, any permitted deductions and how delivery charges are handled. Bank or card-provider processing may add time after the retailer issues a refund.

Need help?

Accessibility statement

The steps taken to make product information and navigation easier to use across devices and assistive technologies.

Our approach

This design aims to provide a clear heading structure, keyboard-accessible navigation, visible focus styles, descriptive image text, readable colour contrast and layouts that reflow on smaller screens. Motion is reduced when a device requests reduced motion, and core information is available without relying on colour alone.

Using this website

You should be able to zoom the page, move through links and controls with a keyboard, and use current screen-reading software to understand the main content. The menu, pack selector, gallery and basket preview have accessible names and states.

Known limitations

The current basket is a design preview rather than a live checkout. Accessibility must be retested after the site is rebuilt in WordPress and WooCommerce, because the theme, plugins, payment fields, cookie banner and third-party services can change keyboard and screen-reader behaviour.

Alternative formats and feedback

If information is difficult to access, the live retailer should offer a way to request it in a suitable alternative format and report a barrier. A working accessibility contact and response target must be added before the store begins trading.

Ongoing review

The live store should be tested with keyboard navigation, text resizing, narrow screens and common assistive technologies after significant theme or plugin changes. Last reviewed for this design: 29 September 2026.
